chapter: Lucky Millinder and Duke Ellington's band, 1948-52
title: His relationship with Ellington and the two raises
summary: Ellington talked quietly with Jackson, and when he tried to quit twice Duke kept him until he agreed to a raise, partly because Basie asked him to join.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: So tell me more about it. What was your relationship with him, Butter?

My relationship was beautiful with him. He loved trombones. He always loved trombones. And a lot of times he used to come and talk to me about quiet things. You know, things -- he asked my -- even -- I can't say he asked my advice. He would talk to me sometimes to see my reaction to different things, you know. The man was a brilliant man. He was a mental giant. You couldn't outtalk him. I tried to
quit the band twice. He kept me up in the Paramount Theater once for an hour after the show closed. And there's no way in the world he'd let me go and so I finally got a raise.
That's twice I got a raise that way, and both times Basie asked me to come with his band and that's what got me the raise both times. I can talk about that now, you know.
